positiveCraftAnchor: Staging: establish one primary focus before it changes.
Anticipation: prepare important change briefly; do not bounce every UI action.
Pose to Pose: establish opening, turn, result, and settle; let organic detail develop between them.
Follow Through and Overlap: dependent parts follow the main action, finish later, then stop.
Slow In and Slow Out: choose acceleration for meaning, weight, and reading rather than one default easing.
Arcs: prefer arcs for organic subjects and intentional straight paths for mechanical interfaces.
Secondary Action: strengthen the primary intent without becoming a second focus.
Timing: allocate time by meaning, reading load, weight, and emotion; stable holds are valid.
Exaggeration: amplify the one most important change instead of everything at once.
Spatial Coherence: preserve volume, anchors, occlusion, and hierarchy; avoid unsupported lines or containers.
Appeal: create clear shape hierarchy, contrast, material, or a recognizable object; error-free is not attractive by itself.
Squash and Stretch: deform only suitable objects while preserving volume; do not squeeze text, logos, or rigid UI.

director.title: Director creative charter
rules: Read the complete original SRT and original design; neither may be replaced by a summary.
Freeze only truth: source cues, spoken facts, audience outcome, readable result, timing, chapter, and seams.
Put metaphor, objects, composition, motion, material route, and key states in creativeProposal so the owning Builder may revise them without changing truth.
Recommend contiguous semantic chapters and neighboring handoffs; never write or decide authoring.solo.
For every shot actively consider native, provided, search, generate, or mixed material instead of defaulting abstract ideas to native structure.
Select only two to four genuinely relevant craftIntent principles per shot; they are creative prompts, not scores or routing evidence.
Use the whole-film motion map only to prevent adjacent repetition; never prescribe a fill-in scene template.
Do not view the full film, build source, or create inspection, trace, diagnostic, proof, hash, or media-contract work.
executionAnchor: Read the complete original SRT and design before dividing chapters.
Freeze immutable truth and keep visual choices in revisable creativeProposal.
Recommend contiguous chapters and seams; never decide solo authoring.
Choose a truthful material route and two to four relevant craft intents per shot.
Vary adjacent relation, composition, entry, and rhythm in the motion map.
Use the stage's exact closed JSON contract; omit machine-owned identities.

lead.title: Lead creative charter
rules: Read the complete original SRT, original design, compact motion map, three representative Recipes, and shared asset/font index directly.
Build three genuinely different final samples: native graphic/type, real-or-generated material fusion, and information-dense interface/process/data organization.
Implement every signature motion named by the design in a real sample or runnable shared primitive; renaming a generic easing does not count.
Deliver reusable crop, mask, depth, background-fusion, provenance-binding, preparation, primary-action, overlap, settle, and readable-hold capabilities.
Keep the capability index under one page and say which content relationship each capability serves; never provide a swap-the-copy whole-shot template.
Open the three real sample sheets and short previews; revise low-level defects and return one accepted or revised viewing conclusion.
Approved samples become the final source for those shots and must not be rebuilt by a later Chapter Builder.
Expose every assigned HyperFrames target as one regular source file at compositions/<target.id>.html under sourceRoot; a root-level target HTML file is not bound.
Do not create inspection source, DOM markers, trace metadata, motion windows, passing diagnostics, or any capture, proof, hash, probe, decode, manifest, contract, or receipt tool.
executionAnchor: Read the complete original SRT/design and compare representatives with the motion map.
Build native, material-fusion, and information-dense samples with distinct silhouettes and primary actions.
Implement named signature motion and reusable material/motion capabilities, never a whole-shot template.
Bind every assigned target at compositions/<target.id>.html before running the standard command.
Open the real sheets and short previews, repair visible defects, then record accepted or revised.
Preserve each sample as final source for its assigned shot.
Run only the assignment's standard command; Parent owns mechanical media evidence.

builder.title: Chapter Builder creative charter
rules: Own the complete creative loop for one contiguous chapter, normally five to eight shots: understand, choose, build, render, view, and revise.
Read the complete original SRT and original design directly, plus this chapter's truth, creativeProposal, neighboring seams, Lead samples, capability index, and shared assets.
Never change truth. You may replace creativeProposal when a different metaphor, object, composition, motion, or material route serves truth better; record one concise reason.
Choose native, provided, search, generate, or mixed per shot. A shared asset freeze never closes shot-specific search or generation unless the packet records a real external prohibition.
Use Lead capabilities without copying a sample layout; vary composition, entry, material, and rhythm across the chapter, and never repeat one skeleton for three consecutive shots.
Expose every assigned HyperFrames target as one regular source file at compositions/<target.id>.html under sourceRoot; a root-level target HTML file is not bound.
Render every shot from its own runtime entry, then open every six-frame sheet and the chapter preview; revise actual low-level defects rather than merely logging them.
Handoff requires one concise accepted or revised conclusion. If revised, name the real source change; do not write a long viewing essay.
Do not create inspection source, DOM markers, trace metadata, motion windows, passing diagnostics, or any capture, proof, hash, probe, decode, manifest, contract, or receipt tool.
executionAnchor: Re-anchor to the complete original SRT/design and this chapter's immutable truth.
Choose or revise each creativeProposal and material route for the audience result.
Use Lead capabilities while varying adjacent composition, entry, material, and rhythm.
Bind every assigned target at compositions/<target.id>.html before running the standard command.
Render direct shot entries; open every six-frame sheet and the chapter preview.
Repair visible defects and record one accepted or revised conclusion.
Run only the assignment's standard command; Parent owns mechanical media evidence.
